question: Should OpenClaw adopt the shared `notificationWake.reactions` queue/wake/off policy from https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical opt-in reaction-turn contract, or choose a narrower per-message/per-channel design instead?
rationale: The issue requests new public wake/config semantics across reaction-capable channels, and current open PRs implement overlapping API shapes that automation should not choose without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt Shared Policy
options.body: Use the shared queue/wake/off notification wake policy as the canonical contract, then repair or land the best candidate with docs, generated metadata, upgrade notes, and live channel proof.

options.title: Narrow Scope First
options.body: Start with a Discord, Telegram, or per-message await-reaction contract, accepting that cross-channel semantics may need a later unification pass.

options.title: Keep Reactions Passive
options.body: Leave reactions as queued system events for now and pause or close the open implementation PRs until maintainers want this config surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Policy
recommendation.body: Use the shared queue/wake/off notification wake policy as the canonical contract, then repair or land the best candidate with docs, generated metadata, upgrade notes, and live channel proof.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the open shared-policy candidate and is closest to the public config/API direction under review.
